issues.description: The problem statement text refers to a method named getFeedingSound() for animals (e.g., "getFeedingSound() should return 'Arf Arf!'"), while the UML, task descriptions elsewhere, the template expectations, and the solution use an abstract method named messageOnFeed(). This name mismatch between getFeedingSound() and messageOnFeed() is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about which method to implement and test against.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either change the problem statement text to refer to messageOnFeed() everywhere (recommended, to match the UML and solution), or rename the abstract method and all implementations in template and solution to getFeedingSound(). Update examples and test descriptions accordingly so students clearly know which method to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement uses two different method names for the same concept: the UML and earlier task specification declare an abstract method messageOnFeed(), but later in the task descriptions the name getFeedingSound() is used when specifying the feeding sound for Seal, Pig, and Goat. The solution implements messageOnFeed(), so the mixed names in the problem text create a naming mismatch that can confuse students about which method to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Prefer using messageOnFeed() (as in the UML and solution): replace all occurrences of getFeedingSound() in the problem statement (and any tests) with messageOnFeed(), or alternatively rename the abstract method in the UML/solution to getFeedingSound()—but ensure all descriptions, templates, tests, and solution use the same identifier.
